instructions.name: depth-before-size
instructions.title: Deeper, not bigger
instructions.text: Before you write the plan, answer in a few lines: what would an expert in this field do here that the brief doesn't ask for; what is the rawest material to start from (the real failing output, the files, the logs) instead of a summary; which methods and tools would they use; and what, other than you or the user, shows the result is right (name the artifact). Put the answers at the top of the plan as choices the user can take or leave.

instructions.name: draw-system
instructions.title: Draw the system map
instructions.text: Draw the parts of the system this plan builds or changes, and nothing else, in "system" on define: parts (id, name, parent, desc, files), lines (from, to, says) and people (actors). Put a part inside another with "parent". Something outside the project, such as Redis or a service in another repo, is a part with kind "outside" and evidence: seen (the file and the text in it), said (what the user told you) or guess. Sentinel checks every seen citation and turns one that fails into a guess. Each state names the parts it builds in "parts": parts with nothing inside them. A state that only reads, or comes from a flow, names none. Sentinel sets every status itself, so do not say what is built or tested.

instructions.name: fast-checks
instructions.title: Fastest check that proves it
instructions.text: Give each state the fastest check that proves its own work: one test file, a type check or a build. Run the whole suite once, in the last state.

instructions.name: failure-list
instructions.title: Failure list first
instructions.text: Before writing logic, write down how it can fail and test each item, with the tests written before the code. Tests written after the code to raise coverage end up restating it.

instructions.name: quote-the-source
instructions.title: Each state quotes what asked for it
instructions.text: Sentinel compares each state's quote with the plan you approved and the messages you typed, word for word and with no model. A quote that isn't there is refused, and a state nothing asked for shows as Claude's addition.

instructions.name: fails-first
instructions.title: Check fails before the work
instructions.text: Sentinel runs the state's check once before any edit. If it already passes, Claude is told the check proves nothing yet and tightens it.

instructions.name: break-it-once
instructions.title: A test must be able to fail
instructions.text: Break the code each new test targets once and watch the test fail, then put the code back. Report any test you couldn't make fail.

instructions.name: fails-without-change
instructions.title: Check fails without the change
instructions.text: Before a state closes, Sentinel reruns its check in a scratch copy that has the state's test changes but not its code changes. If the check still passes there, the advance is refused until the check is tightened or Claude records why with a decide about this check. If it fails, Sentinel runs it once more with the code changes in, to tell a real failure from a copy that can't run the check.

instructions.name: prove-end-to-end
instructions.title: Prove it end to end
instructions.text: A feature that crosses parts ends with an end-to-end run that leaves an artifact anyone can rerun and a script can check: the command and its saved output, a rendered image, a log.

instructions.name: overseer
instructions.title: Look in when a state runs long or stays stuck
instructions.cost: A read-only Opus agent each time a state passes a mark, and once more at a stuck mark that lasts past its first note. In a small repo one look took 4,000 to 8,000 tokens of output and read 280,000 to 460,000 from the cache.
instructions.text: When a state's working time passes 30 minutes, then 1, 2 and 4 hours, Sentinel starts a read-only Opus agent that looks at it from outside. It answers FINE, FASTER or WRONG, and only FASTER and WRONG reach Claude. The run never stops for it. A stuck mark that lasts past its first note gets one look too, answered WRONG or FINE; FINE lifts the mark. Switched off, the log still notes the time and no agent starts.

instructions.name: measure-before-delete
instructions.title: Delete tests only after measuring
instructions.needs: A mutation-testing tool, such as Stryker or go-mutesting.
instructions.text: Delete a test only after a mutation run shows it catches nothing the others don't. Never by reading alone.

instructions.name: sources-first
instructions.title: Plan from the raw sources
instructions.text: Plan from the raw sources (the TRD, the design frames, the sprint sheet), not summaries of them. Where they disagree, the TRD decides behaviour and data, the design decides screens, and the sprint sheet decides scope and order. List each conflict at the top of the plan, and ask before departing from the TRD on anything structural.

instructions.name: state-settings
instructions.title: Settings per state
instructions.text: You may set what each state needs, where it differs from the plan. define and revise take these fields though the plan tool's schema doesn't list them. On a state: weight (light, standard or thorough) with weightWhy, one line on why, or weightQuote, the user's words; and adds, a list of { name, why } naming Library instructions that fire per state. On the plan: settings, a list of { weight } or { name, on }, each with why or quote. A quote is compared with what the user typed: for an instruction turned on or a stricter weight, its name and one more word will do; anything looser needs at least 5 words that name it. A stricter setting applies with its reason shown. A looser one with only a reason waits for the user on the draft; hands-free it goes through and is listed for them. Leave alone a state that fits the plan.

instructions.name: depth-before-size
instructions.title: Deeper, not bigger
instructions.text: Before you write the plan, answer in a few lines: what would an expert in this field do here that the brief doesn't ask for; what is the rawest material to start from (the real failing output, the files, the logs) instead of a summary; which methods and tools would they use; and what, other than you or the user, shows the result is right (name the artifact). Put the answers at the top of the plan as choices the user can take or leave.

instructions.name: draw-system
instructions.title: Draw the system map
instructions.text: Draw the parts of the system this plan builds or changes, and nothing else, in "system" on define: parts (id, name, parent, desc, files), lines (from, to, says) and people (actors). Put a part inside another with "parent". Something outside the project, such as Redis or a service in another repo, is a part with kind "outside" and evidence: seen (the file and the text in it), said (what the user told you) or guess. Sentinel checks every seen citation and turns one that fails into a guess. Each state names the parts it builds in "parts": parts with nothing inside them. A state that only reads, or comes from a flow, names none. Sentinel sets every status itself, so do not say what is built or tested.

instructions.name: fast-checks
instructions.title: Fastest check that proves it
instructions.text: Give each state the fastest check that proves its own work: one test file, a type check or a build. Run the whole suite once, in the last state.

instructions.name: failure-list
instructions.title: Failure list first
instructions.text: Before writing logic, write down how it can fail and test each item, with the tests written before the code. Tests written after the code to raise coverage end up restating it.

instructions.name: quote-the-source
instructions.title: Each state quotes what asked for it
instructions.text: Sentinel compares each state's quote with the plan you approved and the messages you typed, word for word and with no model. A quote that isn't there is refused, and a state nothing asked for shows as Claude's addition.

instructions.name: fails-first
instructions.title: Check fails before the work
instructions.text: Sentinel runs the state's check once before any edit. If it already passes, Claude is told the check proves nothing yet and tightens it.

instructions.name: break-it-once
instructions.title: A test must be able to fail
instructions.text: Break the code each new test targets once and watch the test fail, then put the code back. Report any test you couldn't make fail.

instructions.name: fails-without-change
instructions.title: Check fails without the change
instructions.text: Before a state closes, Sentinel reruns its check in a scratch copy that has the state's test changes but not its code changes. If the check still passes there, the advance is refused until the check is tightened or Claude records why with a decide about this check. If it fails, Sentinel runs it once more with the code changes in, to tell a real failure from a copy that can't run the check.

instructions.name: prove-end-to-end
instructions.title: Prove it end to end
instructions.text: A feature that crosses parts ends with an end-to-end run that leaves an artifact anyone can rerun and a script can check: the command and its saved output, a rendered image, a log.

instructions.name: overseer
instructions.title: Look in when a state runs long or stays stuck
instructions.cost: A read-only Opus agent each time a state passes a mark, and once more at a stuck mark that lasts past its first note. In a small repo one look took 4,000 to 8,000 tokens of output and read 280,000 to 460,000 from the cache.
instructions.text: When a state's working time passes 30 minutes, then 1, 2 and 4 hours, Sentinel starts a read-only Opus agent that looks at it from outside. It answers FINE, FASTER or WRONG, and only FASTER and WRONG reach Claude. The run never stops for it. A stuck mark that lasts past its first note gets one look too, answered WRONG or FINE; FINE lifts the mark. Switched off, the log still notes the time and no agent starts.

instructions.name: measure-before-delete
instructions.title: Delete tests only after measuring
instructions.needs: A mutation-testing tool, such as Stryker or go-mutesting.
instructions.text: Delete a test only after a mutation run shows it catches nothing the others don't. Never by reading alone.

instructions.name: sources-first
instructions.title: Plan from the raw sources
instructions.text: Plan from the raw sources (the TRD, the design frames, the sprint sheet), not summaries of them. Where they disagree, the TRD decides behaviour and data, the design decides screens, and the sprint sheet decides scope and order. List each conflict at the top of the plan, and ask before departing from the TRD on anything structural.

instructions.name: state-settings
instructions.title: Settings per state
instructions.text: You may set what each state needs, where it differs from the plan. define and revise take these fields though the plan tool's schema doesn't list them. On a state: weight (light, standard or thorough) with weightWhy, one line on why, or weightQuote, the user's words; and adds, a list of { name, why } naming Library instructions that fire per state. On the plan: settings, a list of { weight } or { name, on }, each with why or quote. A quote is compared with what the user typed: for an instruction turned on or a stricter weight, its name and one more word will do; anything looser needs at least 5 words that name it. A stricter setting applies with its reason shown. A looser one with only a reason waits for the user on the draft; hands-free it goes through and is listed for them. Leave alone a state that fits the plan.

flows.name: review
flows.description: Lint, then a review you sign off

states.label: Lint the change
states.title: The change passes lint
states.approach: Run the linter and fix what it finds.

states.label: Review the diff
states.title: You read the change
states.problem: Some mistakes only a reader catches.
states.approach: Walk you through the diff and wait for your OK.

flows.name: changelog
flows.description: Note the change for the next release

flows.name: close-phase
flows.description: Close a phase: check it against the project rules, review it with three agents, fix what you accept, update the docs.

states.label: Re-read the project's rules and design docs, and list where this plan's changes depart from them
states.title: Check against the project rules

states.label: Review the files this plan changed with three agents (simplicity, bugs, project conventions), and list the findings
states.title: Review the changes

states.label: Fix the findings the user accepted
states.title: Fix the accepted findings

states.label: Update the docs this plan made stale
states.title: Update the docs
